walkthrough: Goal: copy a picture that is not square against a frame of its own shape. Before, a portrait painting, a wide film still or a photographed object lay inside the square original frame with blank margins round it while my frame was the whole square, so the picture's edge and my square disagreed and I did not know what to copy against. Now both frames are the picture: the original's cropped exactly to it, mine the same shape and size beside it, so one edge measures both. A single shape's busy photographic ground is faded towards the paper, so I read the object by its negative space against the frame, as V大 means, the ground still faint for context.

The pack: Import practice pack… in the practice options, a pack of two shapes whose pictures are not square chosen (an upright vase and a long fish, both on a studio sweep). A lesson of Single shapes at level 1 from the home lays one shape, its How first.

Single shapes 1/1, the upright vase: the original's frame is the picture exactly, upright, three quarters as wide as it is tall; my frame beside it the same size, empty, the pair held together in the middle of its place on the sheet. The vase stands at full strength, the sweep round it faded towards the paper (to 30 %), still there as a pale ground. I draw its outline with Draw, its belly a little wide on the right. Compare: the picture laid exactly over my frame, edge on edge, at 35 % with its outline in see-through red, my ink through it, the wide belly plain; Aligned moves and sizes the outline onto my copy as one shape; In place again.
The long fish (Simple) is not laid here: lessons of Single shapes at level 1 lay the vase (Entry) each time while it is kept, so this walk no longer reaches a wide shape.

Back later: the app ends and starts again; the lesson reopens on its sheet as I left it, my outline on the vase in the frame of its shape (the canvas as before), no How this time; a pinch shows both frames; Compare.

Divisions: the composition pack imported, a lesson of Divisions at level 1, its How's example now in frames of the landscape's shape, no pencil edge. A landscape: both frames its shape, wide and low; my frame is the picture's edge. I divide it: the field's edge and the ridge in red, the house's frame and the tree's upright green, the path blue. Compare lays the picture exactly over my frame under my lines; the table: Main 2 lines, 100 % (the frame's width, the picture's longer side). Next, Next, Finish.

Value masses: Finish, That's all for today, a lesson of Value masses at level 1, its How in frames of the picture's shape. The first, a landscape: Middle and Fill frame fill my frame, the picture's shape, whole; Dark on the tree; Light on the sky's upper two rows, the house and the path. Compare lays the answer's greys exactly over my frame, its mass edges red, hatched light where I left the sky's lower strip middle, and a little of the path's foot. Finish, That's all for today, a second lesson of Value masses: an upright landscape, its frames tall and narrow; Middle and Fill frame, Light on the sky, the house and the path, Dark on the tree; Compare alike, the hatching where the sky's right and the ridge's corner were left middle. Finish, That's all for today.
The upright composition for a division is not laid here: a second lesson of Divisions (level 1 or 2) lays the other landscape, so this walk no longer divides a tall frame.

A whole copy: a lesson of Whole copies at level 1, the other landscape (the tree left, the house right); its division in red, then Draw (the division dimmed) the house and the tree; Compare the picture exactly over my frame of its shape, my house drawn a little high.

Not here: the author's eye on the tablet (how faded the ground should be: kept, faded more or less, or dropped); objects' pictures, which stay square; a colour copy, whose frames always were its picture's.
